‘Gold is no silver bullet' and isn't hedging against equity drawdowns, but ‘debasement trade' should continue – HSBC
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold will continue to benefit from the debasement trade despite its recent weakness, but precious metals investors would do well to diversify, as the yellow metal hasn’t provided effective protection against recent stock market pullbacks, according to market strategists at HSBC Asset Management. “Gold’s spectacular bull run, which saw prices climb to well above USD5,000 per ounce earlier this year, has fizzled out,” they said in a recent report. “Prices are down and volatility is up. Should investors throw in the towel?” The strategists caution that while gold has underperformed since the early-year rally amid sky-high oil prices, rising rates, and soaring bond yields, “there is still a compelling strategic rationale for the metal in portfolios as geopolitical fragmentation and central bank reserve diversification keep demand supported.”

items.titleEn: Gold, silver pressured despite lower yields as Hormuz attacks send crude higher - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Thursday, as renewed attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and rising Middle East tensions pushed crude oil prices higher, reinforcing inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Precious metals failed to benefit from lower Treasury yields and defensive demand as the prospect of persistently elevated interest rates continued to weigh on bullion. At the latest verified morning price reading, spot gold was near $4,086.90 an ounce, down $53.40, or 1.29%, while spot silver was near $55.790, down $2.070, or 3.57%. The latest U.S. labor-market figures provided another indication of economic resilience despite high borrowing costs and weakening housing activity. Weekly initial jobless claims declined by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 in the week ended Oct. 17, below expectations of approximately 200,000 and down from the previous week's upwardly revised 200,000. The four-week moving average fell by 1,000 to 197,750. Continuing claims increased by 25,000 to 1.728 million in the week ended Oct. 10, while the insured unemployment rate remained unchanged at 1.1%. The decline in new claims suggests layoffs remain limited, although rising continuing claims indicate that unemployed workers may be taking longer to find new jobs. Market positioning continues to favor an October pause followed by additional monetary tightening before year-end. Traders assign a high probability to no change at the Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting, while the likelihood of a 25-basis-point increase in December remains around 86%. Thursday's stronger-than-expected jobless claims reinforced the view that the labor market has not weakened enough to force an immediate change in policy, while rising energy prices are intensifying concerns about the inflation outlook. Treasury yields nevertheless declined as renewed selling in technology stocks and escalating Middle East tensions supported demand for government bonds. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell toward the 5.0% area, providing some relief from recent highs, although gold remained under selling pressure. The decline underscores the continuing importance of Fed rate expectations and portfolio positioning relative to traditional safe-haven demand.

items.titleEn: Gold prices under pressure as US weekly jobless claims fall to three-month low
Gold prices struggling as U.S. weekly jobless claims fall to three-month low
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is struggling below $4,100 an ounce and could face further selling pressure as the U.S. labor market remains relatively healthy, with fewer American workers applying for unemployment benefits than expected. Initial claims for state unemployment benefits came in at a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ending October 17, the Labor Department announced Thursday. The number was below expectations, as consensus estimates forecast a steady 200,000 claims. The previous week’s figure was revised up to 200,000. Spot gold has been on the back foot through most of the European session, and while prices have recovered from their session lows, the market continues to face significant selling pressure. Gold last traded at $4,076 an ounce, down 1.5% on the day.
